clue.text: See 9
Explosive type wanted unlimited turns

indicators.note: turns means the trimmed letters are read backwards
unlimited means without limits, so the word wanted loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A demolition expert is sought for a job with endless twists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips wanted to ANTE, and 'turns' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano erupts often, so it is an explosive type in the volcanic sense.

clue.text: Alternative arrival time in Central America — ready for Nicaragua?

indicators.note: in means the other pieces go inside the abbreviation for Central America

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for Central America
or introduces an alternative
DOB, date of birth, is the time of one's arrival in the world

explanation.surface: Another arrival time in Central America, with a query about Nicaragua being prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for cash, which is why the definition is currency rather than readiness.
explanation.definitionFit: The cordoba is the national currency of Nicaragua, and 'ready' is slang for money.

clue.text: Puritan holding shit stick out

indicators.note: holding means the word for a puritan contains the other piece

parts.note: a prude is a prim, puritanical person
shit as in nonsense is rot

explanation.surface: A puritan, faced with filth, decides to stick it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To project beyond a surface is the plain meaning of both phrases: a synonym.

clue.text: Hypocritical time with one's daughter

parts.note: one's means belonging to one, and one is an ace, so 'of ace'

explanation.surface: Someone spends time with their daughter while being a hypocrite.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 'one's' as a possessive: 'of one', with ace standing for one as on dice and cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deceitfully showing two different faces to people is a hypocrite: a synonym.

clue.text: British rockers would like celebrated dandy reported

parts.note: to wish is to want or would like

indicators.note: reported means the dandy's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Beau Nash was the famous Regency-era dandy who ran society in Bath

explanation.surface: British rock musicians want a famous dandy, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishbone Ash are an English rock band formed in 1969, famous for twin lead guitars.

clue.text: See 13
To reduce severity of the punishment, make AC/DC split the daily journey

definitions.text: To reduce severity of the punishment
definitions.meaning: a sentence can be lessened, as a death sentence to life imprisonment
in electrics this means to reverse current, as a split-ring commutator turns alternating into direct
the regular trip to and from work

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the AC/DC sense is electrical engineering, not the rock band, and a split-ring commutator does the conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessening a sentence, switching current direction and the regular trip to work are three senses of one verb and noun.

clue.text: Avoid folding over Bill, maybe cutting direct debit?

indicators.note: cutting means the pieces slice into the abbreviation for direct debit

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
Bill and Ben are the Flowerpot Men of British children's TV, so Bill might be 'not Ben'

explanation.surface: A warning about creasing a bill paid by direct debit.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben were puppets in a 1950s British children's TV show, so Bill is the one who is 'not Ben'.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed instruction on envelopes holding photos or certificates tells handlers not to crease them.

clue.text: New arrival is thankful for cloak that was close!

parts.note: arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrival
someone thankful for a favour owes the giver, so this phrase gives owes
a cape is a sleeveless cloak

explanation.surface: A newborn's parent is grateful for a shawl, exclaiming at a close shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is thankful for' becomes OWES: you owe thanks to whoever did you a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclaiming 'that was close!' describes a lucky near miss, a scrape survived by the smallest margin.

clue.text: A boy's name that's rejected unanimously

parts.note: a boy is a son

indicators.note: rejected suggests being turned back, so the word name is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy's name is turned down by everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting all together, with nobody dissenting, is the idiom's meaning: everyone in agreement.

clue.text: Our guy Mark is copper sustained by a little cookie

indicators.note: sustained by means held up within, so the pieces sit inside the word for a little

parts.note: a bit is a little
taken as written
bo is American slang for a fellow or guy
NB, nota bene, means mark well
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A man called Mark is a policeman kept going by a small biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is the metal, not a policeman. A BOURBON BISCUIT is a British chocolate sandwich biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: This chocolate-cream sandwich biscuit is a British example of a cookie.

clue.text: Particular punches a jolly exhausting way to win bout

indicators.note: punches means the detail pierces the word for a jolly

parts.note: a jolly is a fun trip, an outing
a point is a particular, a detail

explanation.surface: A specific person throws punches on a tiring day out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhausting' belongs to the definition: a points win means boxing the full, tiring distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning a boxing match on the judges' scores, without a knockout, means going all rounds.

clue.text: King George and National I find thrilling — this is what's in store?

definitions.text: King George and National I find thrilling — this is what's in store?

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
taken as written

indicators.note: in means the other pieces go inside the word for a store

parts.note: a stash is a hidden store

indicators.note: thrilling means excited, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A racegoer says the King George and Grand National races excite them, wondering if more is to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrilling' rearranges I FIND; 'in' marks the container. The King George VI Chase and the Grand National are famous British horse races, so the whole clue paints the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciting close end to a race, as at those big races, is a spectacular finale awaiting the crowd.

clue.text: Workman equally suited to G&T sups with Her Majesty

indicators.note: sups means drinks in, so the G and T take the other pieces inside

parts.note: the letters G and T
as means equally, as in as big
fit means suitable
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A tradesman fit to drink gin and tonic with the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who installs and repairs gas appliances is a kind of workman.

clue.text: See 16
Pass round fliers ready for Banksy work?

indicators.note: round means the word for pass surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to go is to pass, as time goes by
the RAF, Royal Air Force, are fliers
fit means ready, in condition

explanation.surface: An instruction to pass round flyers prepared for an artist's show.
explanation.walkthrough: Banksy is the anonymous British street artist known for stencilled wall art.
explanation.definitionFit: A single piece of wall art scrawled or sprayed in public is an example of the street artist's work.

clue.text: #metoo: it just takes the chap in

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is 'it' in crossword usage

indicators.note: takes with in means the word for just holds the other piece inside
in completes takes ... in, meaning to contain

parts.note: mere means just, nothing more
he is the chap

explanation.surface: A comment on the #MeToo movement involving only drawing a man in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition ignores the hashtag movement: 'me too' simply means the speaker agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'me too' expresses agreement that one shares the same experience: an idiom.

clue.text: Fish: tick in order first and second choices from your menu, circling one

indicators.note: circling means the other pieces go round the word one

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a mo

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word your
second choices from takes the second letter of the word menu

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner ticks off their picks in order on a menu, ringing one item.
explanation.definitionFit: The mooneye is a North American freshwater fish with notably large eyes.

clue.text: See 20
Pampered realm in which to serve?

definitions.text: Pampered realm in which to serve?

indicators.note: in which means the word for serve goes inside the reworked letters
pampered suggests fussed over and messed about, so the letters of realm are rearranged

parts.note: to do is to serve, as in that will do

explanation.surface: A cosseted kingdom where one might serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pampered' scrambles the letters of realm, and 'in which' marks the container; the whole clue also describes an earl's domain.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl's territory was a domain where tenants and retainers served their lord, a pampered realm.

clue.text: A fad involving fitting of foreskin-ring: should this worry me — sorry, him?

definitions.text: should this worry me — sorry, him?

indicators.note: fitting means putting the pieces together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone worries about a trendy genital piercing, then pretends it is about another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitting of' rearranges A FAD plus FORESKIN RING.
explanation.definitionFit: The jokey phrase pretends an embarrassing question is on another person's behalf, when it is really the speaker's own.

clue.text: Responsibilities of those collecting fine in press function

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes

indicators.note: in means those letters go inside the word for a function

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

indicators.note: collecting means the word for 'of those' gathers the other piece inside

parts.note: their means of those, belonging to them
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: The duties of people collecting a penalty at a press event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press function' looks like a media event, but it is two pieces: the verb press and a maths function, with 'collecting' and 'in' marking two containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Having several projects on the go at once is the idiom's meaning: a set of commitments.

clue.text: The last word in steam engines

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words steam engines

explanation.surface: A claim about the ultimate in steam locomotives.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken at the end of a prayer or hymn, it is literally the closing word.

clue.text: A failing that, staying over 8 furlongs? Too much

indicators.note: staying means holding, so the trimmed word keeps the other piece inside
failing means going missing, so the letter A drops out of that

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for 8 furlongs reads backwards

parts.note: eight furlongs make one mile in horse racing, written I MILE with the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A racing tip about a horse weak at the end, staying beyond a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' removes A from THAT, giving THT; 'over' reverses I MILE (one mile) to ELIMI, which THT holds by 'staying'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is the absolute end, beyond what can be borne, means it is excessive: an idiom.

clue.text: See 26
Get back on job, not initially 'plum'

indicators.note: not initially means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a greengage is a variety of plum

explanation.surface: An instruction to return to a cushy job, though not at first a plum one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plum' looks like 'a plum job' but is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire someone again, or resume a task, is to take them back into work.

clue.text: Comic, this tactical nous behind King Harold's downfall?

definitions.meaning: a comedian; the British slapstick film comedian of that name

definitions.text: tactical nous behind King Harold's downfall?
definitions.meaning: the cleverness of the invaders from northern France who beat Harold at Hastings in 1066

explanation.surface: A comedian's tactical sense is credited with toppling an English king.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Wisdom was a British slapstick comedian; William of Normandy beat King Harold at Hastings in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian's name doubles as the shrewdness of William's army, whose feigned retreat defeated Harold.
